description: A climbing foliage plant with large split leaves. Give it space and a sturdy support; younger leaves may have fewer holes.

description: A trailing or climbing plant with heart-shaped leaves, often marked with gold. A useful choice for shelves and hanging pots.
sunlightInstructions: Filtered daylight supports good growth. Lower light is tolerated; avoid scorching direct sun.
wateringInstructions: Allow the mix to dry between thorough waterings, and empty the outer pot. Growth slows in winter.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth, following a suitable product label; reduce or pause when growth slows. Add and adjust a reminder if needed.
soilInstructions: Use a freely draining indoor potting mix in a pot with drainage holes.
humidityInstructions: Ordinary indoor humidity is tolerated; protect from cold drafts.

growthReferences.title: Compact potted foliage
growthReferences.description: This specimen has short visible stems and heart-shaped, variegated leaves. Pothos grown in containers commonly retains this juvenile leaf shape; leaf colour patterns alone do not indicate age.

growthReferences.title: Trailing stems
growthReferences.description: This separate specimen shows long stems hanging below its pot. Pothos can trail or climb with aerial roots. Stem length and leaf size depend on support, light and growing conditions, rather than a fixed timetable.

description: An upright succulent with stiff, patterned leaves. Also sold under its former name, Sansevieria trifasciata.
sunlightInstructions: A bright position is useful, but it tolerates lower light. Introduce stronger sun gradually.
wateringInstructions: Let the potting mix dry before watering. In winter it may need water only every month or two; check first.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth, following a suitable product label; reduce or pause when growth slows. Add and adjust a reminder if needed.
soilInstructions: Use a very well-drained succulent mix and a pot that releases excess water.
humidityInstructions: Tolerates dry room air. Keep out of frost and cold, wet conditions.

description: A slow-growing plant with glossy leaflets and water-storing rhizomes. Too much water is a greater risk than an occasional missed check.
sunlightInstructions: Bright indirect daylight is ideal; lower light is tolerated. Protect from hot direct sun.
wateringInstructions: Water only after the mix dries. Winter checks may be spaced further apart; do not water a still-damp pot.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth, following a suitable product label; reduce or pause when growth slows. Add and adjust a reminder if needed.
soilInstructions: Choose a well-drained mix and a container with drainage holes.
humidityInstructions: Ordinary indoor humidity is suitable. Keep in a warm room, away from cold windows.

description: A cascading plant with narrow arching leaves and hanging plantlets. Variegated forms are common indoors.
sunlightInstructions: Choose filtered daylight; keep leaves out of strong direct sun.
wateringInstructions: Keep the mix lightly moist rather than saturated. Let the surface begin to dry and reduce watering in winter.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth, following a suitable product label; reduce or pause when growth slows. Add and adjust a reminder if needed.
soilInstructions: Use a moisture-retentive but draining houseplant mix.
humidityInstructions: Average indoor humidity is usually suitable. Keep away from cold drafts.

growthReferences.title: Plant with hanging plantlets

description: An upright indoor tree with thick, glossy leaves. Keep its position stable and handle the irritating milky sap carefully.
sunlightInstructions: Provide bright indirect light, with protection from strong afternoon sun.
wateringInstructions: Check the mix before watering and avoid keeping it continually wet. Water less during slower winter growth.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth, following a suitable product label; reduce or pause when growth slows. Add and adjust a reminder if needed.
soilInstructions: Use a draining houseplant mix and empty any water left in the cover pot.
humidityInstructions: Average room humidity suits it. Avoid drafts and sudden temperature changes.

growthReferences.title: Young variegated specimen
growthReferences.description: This young potted specimen has patterned leaves. Variegation is a cultivar characteristic, not a stage that every rubber plant will develop. Different examples do not establish an age or size target.

photo.title: Young Plant (Cabarrus County,NC)

growthReferences.title: Upright potted form
growthReferences.description: This separate potted specimen shows the upright habit and broad leaves. Pruning and growing conditions affect its shape; indoor plants need not reach the size of outdoor trees.

description: A small indoor tree with slender branches and many pointed leaves. Moving it or changing its light abruptly can cause leaf drop.
sunlightInstructions: Choose a bright, stable position with indirect daylight.
wateringInstructions: Water before the entire root ball dries, while allowing excess water to drain. Check less frequently in winter.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth, following a suitable product label; reduce or pause when growth slows. Add and adjust a reminder if needed.
soilInstructions: Use a well-drained, moisture-retentive indoor potting mix.
humidityInstructions: Protect from cold drafts, heating vents and sudden changes in conditions.

description: A cane-forming foliage plant with broad strap-shaped leaves. Cultivars may have green, cream or yellow striping.
sunlightInstructions: Moderate to bright filtered light works well; harsh sun can damage leaves.
wateringInstructions: Keep the mix moderately moist during active growth, without leaving it waterlogged. Reduce watering in winter.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth, following a suitable product label; reduce or pause when growth slows. Add and adjust a reminder if needed.
soilInstructions: Use a draining indoor potting mix and a pot with drainage holes.
humidityInstructions: Very dry heated air can brown leaf tips. Avoid cold drafts and hot radiators.

description: A group of houseplants with glossy foliage and white flower-like spathes. This entry gives general guidance for common indoor hybrids.
sunlightInstructions: Use filtered daylight or partial shade; avoid direct sun.
wateringInstructions: Keep the mix evenly moist, not soggy. Check the surface and pot weight rather than watering automatically.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth, following a suitable product label; reduce or pause when growth slows. Add and adjust a reminder if needed.
soilInstructions: Use a moisture-retentive houseplant mix that still drains freely.
humidityInstructions: Prefers a warm room with humid air. Keep away from cold drafts.

growthReferences.title: Clumping leafy form

photo.title: Flower

description: Common flowering orchid hybrids with arching stems and long-lasting blooms. Their exposed roots need air as well as moisture.

wateringInstructions: Run tepid water through the bark and drain completely. Let the bark partly dry; avoid water sitting in the crown.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth, following a suitable product label; reduce or pause when growth slows. Add and adjust a reminder if needed.
soilInstructions: Use a bark-based orchid medium, not ordinary dense potting soil.
humidityInstructions: Keep warm with gentle airflow and moderate humidity; avoid cold drafts.

growthReferences.title: Leaves and a flower stem
growthReferences.description: This orchid has strap-shaped leaves and an upright flower stem. Moth orchids are a varied hybrid group, so stem length and plant size can differ substantially.

growthReferences.title: Flowers on an arching spray
growthReferences.description: The flowering example illustrates the moth-like flowers that give this group its common name. Flower colour and bloom timing vary; a resting plant without flowers is not automatically unhealthy.

description: A rosette-forming succulent with fleshy, toothed leaves. Keep it ornamental; this catalog is not guidance for eating or applying plant material.
sunlightInstructions: Provide strong daylight with some sun; introduce brighter conditions gradually.
wateringInstructions: Wait for the mix to dry before watering thoroughly and draining. Water much less during winter.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth, following a suitable product label; reduce or pause when growth slows. Add and adjust a reminder if needed.
soilInstructions: Use a gritty, fast-draining succulent mix and drainage holes.
humidityInstructions: Dry indoor air is suitable. Protect from frost and cold, wet roots.

growthReferences.title: Leaf rosette
growthReferences.description: The thick, pointed leaves grow outward from the centre in a rosette. This specimen illustrates that leaf arrangement; its size does not establish an age or diagnose plant health.

growthReferences.title: Developing flower stalk

description: A branching succulent with rounded, fleshy leaves. Older plants can develop a small tree-like form.
sunlightInstructions: Give it a bright position with some sun, sheltered from very harsh afternoon exposure.
wateringInstructions: Water moderately only when the mix has dried. Reduce watering from autumn through winter.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth, following a suitable product label; reduce or pause when growth slows. Add and adjust a reminder if needed.
soilInstructions: Use a freely draining succulent mix; do not leave water in the saucer.
humidityInstructions: Ordinary dry room air is suitable. Keep protected from frost.

wateringInstructions: Keep the mix lightly moist and well drained; do not keep the roots saturated.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth, following a suitable product label; reduce or pause when growth slows. Add and adjust a reminder if needed.
soilInstructions: Use a light, draining houseplant mix in a pot with drainage holes.
humidityInstructions: Average home humidity is tolerated. Avoid cold drafts and direct heat.

description: A clumping indoor palm with arching feathery fronds. Also commonly sold as Dypsis lutescens; it needs room as it grows.
sunlightInstructions: Provide bright indirect daylight in a warm room.
wateringInstructions: Keep the mix moist but not soggy during growth. Check moisture before watering and drain the pot.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth, following a suitable product label; reduce or pause when growth slows. Add and adjust a reminder if needed.
soilInstructions: Use a well-drained indoor potting mix and a pot that drains freely.
humidityInstructions: Prefers humid air. Dry heating conditions can be challenging; keep away from radiators.

description: A large foliage plant with broad banana-like leaves. It can outgrow a small room; the reference photo shows a mature flowering plant.
sunlightInstructions: Provide a very bright position with filtered daylight.
wateringInstructions: Water after the top layer of mix dries, then let excess water escape. Adjust checks as growth slows.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth, following a suitable product label; reduce or pause when growth slows. Add and adjust a reminder if needed.
soilInstructions: Use a draining, loam-based indoor potting mix in a sturdy pot.
humidityInstructions: Prefers warm, humid conditions. Protect leaves from cold drafts and sudden temperature changes.

soilInstructions: Use an airy, well-drained houseplant mix in a pot with drainage holes.

wateringInstructions: Let the potting mix dry between thorough waterings, then drain fully. Reduce watering during slower growth; do not keep the roots wet.
fertilizingInstructions: Use a suitable fertilizer during active growth according to its label; reduce or pause feeding when growth slows.
soilInstructions: Use a fast-draining succulent mix and a container that releases excess water.
humidityInstructions: Ordinary indoor humidity is suitable. Keep frost-free with good airflow.

wateringInstructions: Let the surface begin to dry, then water and drain. Avoid waterlogged roots; adjust checks when growth and flowering slow.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during spring and summer growth following the product label; reduce or pause feeding in autumn and early winter.
soilInstructions: Use an airy, moisture-retentive but freely draining mix. This forest cactus needs different care from a desert cactus.
humidityInstructions: Prefers humid air with gentle circulation. Avoid abrupt light or temperature changes while buds develop.

sunlightInstructions: Use bright indirect daylight in a cool room, away from hot direct sun.
wateringInstructions: During leafy growth, water at the pot edge or from below when the surface dries, then drain. Keep the crown dry. Reduce water during summer dormancy and resume gradually as new growth returns.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active leafy growth or flowering according to the product label. Stop feeding during dormancy.
soilInstructions: Use a rich, freely draining potting mix; avoid burying or soaking the crown.
humidityInstructions: Keep cool with moderate humidity and gentle airflow. Protect from frost and radiators.

sunlightInstructions: Provide bright indirect daylight. It tolerates a dimmer position, but keep it away from hot direct sun.
wateringInstructions: Let the surface of the mix dry slightly before watering, then drain thoroughly. Avoid leaving the roots in standing water.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed lightly during active spring and summer growth according to the product label. Pause feeding in winter.
soilInstructions: Use a humus-rich houseplant mix with good drainage. Repot only when necessary.

fertilizingInstructions: Feed sparingly during active growth using a suitable houseplant fertilizer at its labelled strength. Reduce or pause in winter.
soilInstructions: Use a rich, freely draining potting mix and a pot with drainage holes.
humidityInstructions: Typical room humidity is suitable. Keep away from cold drafts and drying heat.

wateringInstructions: Allow the top layer of mix to dry before watering, then let excess water drain. Avoid both persistent wetness and prolonged complete drying.
fertilizingInstructions: Use a suitable houseplant fertilizer during active growth following the product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows.
soilInstructions: Use an airy, freely draining houseplant mix. A pot with drainage holes helps prevent waterlogged roots.
humidityInstructions: Average indoor humidity is suitable. Avoid cold drafts and sudden changes in conditions.

fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth, following a suitable houseplant fertilizer label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows.
soilInstructions: Rich, airy potting mix with drainage.
humidityInstructions: Prefers moderate humidity and steady warmth, away from heating vents.

fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth, following a suitable houseplant fertilizer label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows.
soilInstructions: A well-drained bonsai or houseplant mix appropriate to the container.
humidityInstructions: Needs a warm room and humid air; protect from cold drafts.

sunlightInstructions: Use diffuse indirect light. Green forms tolerate lower light; brighter variegated forms need more filtered daylight.
wateringInstructions: Allow the surface to begin drying between waterings, then drain. Reduce watering when growth slows.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth, following a suitable houseplant fertilizer label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows.
soilInstructions: Use a moisture-retentive but well-drained potting mix.
humidityInstructions: Keep warm and away from cold drafts; tolerates ordinary indoor humidity.

photo.altText: Potted specimen of a plant with variegated foliage.
photo.title: Aglaonema modestum as a potted plant.

description: A climbing or trailing plant with arrow-shaped juvenile leaves. Older climbing plants develop differently shaped leaves; cultivars vary in colour.
sunlightInstructions: Bright filtered daylight; direct sun can scorch or bleach foliage.
wateringInstructions: Keep the mix lightly moist as the surface begins drying, then drain excess water.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth, following a suitable houseplant fertilizer label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows.
soilInstructions: Use a rich, freely draining houseplant mix.
humidityInstructions: Prefers a warm room and humid air. A support accommodates its climbing habit.

description: A trailing plant with striped leaves and purple undersides. Pinching back leggy stems encourages a fuller plant; sap can irritate skin.
sunlightInstructions: Bright indirect daylight gives good colour. Introduce any gentle sun gradually and avoid harsh summer sun.
wateringInstructions: Water when the surface of the mix dries, then drain. Reduce watering during slower winter growth.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth, following a suitable houseplant fertilizer label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows.
soilInstructions: A standard, well-drained houseplant mix.
humidityInstructions: Ordinary room humidity is suitable; keep warm and protect from cold drafts.

photo.altText: Potted plant showing silver-striped leaves with purple underside
photo.title: Tradescantia zebrina

description: A climbing or trailing plant with thick leaves and waxy flowers. The photo shows a variegated form; retain old flower spurs because they can bloom again.
sunlightInstructions: Bright indirect daylight throughout the year.
wateringInstructions: Allow the mix to dry between waterings, then drain. Avoid persistent wetness or prolonged drought.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth, following a suitable houseplant fertilizer label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows.
soilInstructions: Use a loose, fast-draining mix suitable for an epiphytic plant.
humidityInstructions: Prefers humid air and warmth. Repot only when needed, avoiding flowering periods.

photo.altText: thick, waxy, variegated leaves of green and creamy white
photo.title: Hoya carnosa, houseplant view

growthReferences.title: Cluster of unopened buds
growthReferences.description: This wax plant carries a cluster of closed flower buds. Bud production depends on the plant and conditions; their absence does not establish that care is wrong.

photo.altText: Wax plant with a hanging cluster of unopened pink buds
photo.title: Flower buds

growthReferences.title: Open star-shaped flowers
growthReferences.description: A different specimen shows a rounded cluster of open, star-shaped flowers. These are reference features, not a before-and-after sequence or a promise of a flowering date.

photo.altText: Wax plant with a rounded cluster of pale star-shaped flowers
photo.title: Umble inflorescence

description: Fine trailing stems carry small heart-shaped leaves and bead-like aerial tubers. Suitable for a hanging pot or small trellis.
sunlightInstructions: Provide bright indirect daylight.
wateringInstructions: Let the mix dry completely between waterings. Water even less during winter rest.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth, following a suitable houseplant fertilizer label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows.
soilInstructions: Use a sandy, freely draining succulent mix and a pot with drainage.
humidityInstructions: Normal indoor humidity is suitable. Avoid cold wet conditions and unnecessary repotting.

photo.altText: Potted vining plant trained on a heart-shaped trellis.
photo.title: Potted plant.

description: A slow-growing plant with a swollen water-storing base and long curling leaves. Despite its common name, it is not a true palm.
sunlightInstructions: Choose a sunny window and acclimatize gradually to stronger light.
wateringInstructions: Let the mix dry between thorough waterings. Reduce water substantially during winter.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth, following a suitable houseplant fertilizer label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows.
soilInstructions: A fast-draining cactus or succulent mix.
humidityInstructions: Tolerates ordinary dry indoor air. Keep warm and prevent water collecting around the base.

description: A small, spreading foliage plant with contrasting white, pink or red leaf veins. Compact forms suit terrariums with appropriate ventilation.
sunlightInstructions: Medium to bright indirect daylight; avoid direct sun.
wateringInstructions: Check frequently and keep the mix evenly moist, draining any excess. Avoid both complete drying and waterlogged roots.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth, following a suitable houseplant fertilizer label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows.
soilInstructions: Use a freely draining, moisture-retentive potting mix in a shallow container.
humidityInstructions: Protect from dry air and drafts. Moderate humidity and gentle airflow help prevent leaf problems.

description: A trailing or climbing vine with heart-shaped leaves. The reference photo shows the variegated Brasil cultivar; it is different from golden pothos.
sunlightInstructions: Medium indirect daylight; tolerates a dimmer position but grows better with filtered light.
wateringInstructions: Keep the mix slightly moist as its surface begins to dry. Reduce watering when winter growth slows.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth, following a suitable houseplant fertilizer label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows.
soilInstructions: Use an airy houseplant mix with reliable drainage.
humidityInstructions: Tolerates normal indoor air, preferring moderate humidity and steady warmth.

photo.altText: Vining houseplant with heart-shaped leaves bearing a stripe.
photo.title: P. hederaceum 'Brasil'

description: A climbing or trailing aroid with perforated leaves. It is a different species from the larger Swiss cheese plant, Monstera deliciosa.
sunlightInstructions: Give bright filtered daylight and protect the leaves from strong direct sun.
wateringInstructions: Keep the root zone lightly moist, allowing the surface to start drying before watering. Drain excess water.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: An airy, organically rich potting mix with good drainage.
humidityInstructions: Warm, humid rooms suit it. Provide a support for climbing and keep away from cold drafts.

photo.title: Monstera adansonii (Swiss Cheese Plant) houseplant view

description: A trailing or climbing vine with silver-patterned leaves. Despite its common name, it is distinct from golden pothos in the genus Epipremnum.
sunlightInstructions: Use bright indirect light, sheltered from harsh sun.
wateringInstructions: Keep the mix lightly moist, letting the surface dry slightly between thorough waterings. Never leave the roots standing in water.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: A loose, well-drained houseplant mix.
humidityInstructions: Keep in a warm room away from drafts. A stake supports climbing; hanging pots let stems trail.

photo.title: Mature plant form grown as trailing houseplant

description: A climbing vine with deeply divided leaves. It resembles a small Monstera but belongs to a different genus, and is not a philodendron.
sunlightInstructions: Bright indirect daylight is best; protect from intense sun.
wateringInstructions: Water when roughly the top inch of mix has dried, then let the pot drain.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: An airy, freely draining houseplant mix.
humidityInstructions: Likes warmth and humid air. Give aerial roots a support and keep out of cold drafts.

description: A cultivated hybrid with arrow-shaped leaves and striking pale veins, formerly called Alocasia x amazonica. The reference photo shows the compact cultivar Polly.
sunlightInstructions: Provide bright indirect daylight; direct sun can scorch the foliage.
wateringInstructions: Keep the mix moist but well drained during growth. Reduce watering when growth slows rather than leaving the roots wet.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: A fertile, airy mix with reliable drainage.
humidityInstructions: Needs warmth and humid air. Protect from cold windows and abrupt temperature changes.

description: A foliage group including Begonia rex and its many hybrids. Leaf patterns and colours vary widely between cultivars; the photo is one example.
sunlightInstructions: Choose bright filtered light, avoiding harsh direct sun.
wateringInstructions: Keep the mix lightly moist with good drainage. Avoid soggy roots and splashing or misting the leaves.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: An organically rich, airy potting mix with drainage.
humidityInstructions: Prefers humid air with good circulation. Remove dead foliage and keep the crown from staying wet.

photo.title: Begonia--Rex Types (Painted Leaf Begonia) houseplant view

description: A feathery ornamental related to asparagus, rather than a true fern. Older scrambling stems can have sharp spines; berries and sap need care around pets.
sunlightInstructions: Bright indirect daylight; strong direct sun can damage the foliage.
wateringInstructions: Keep the mix moist during active growth without waterlogging it. Reduce watering in winter.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: A moisture-retentive but well-drained, organically rich potting mix.
humidityInstructions: Prefers humid air. Watch for dry rooms and allow space for arching or climbing stems.

description: A single-stemmed palm with arching feather-like fronds. Pots may contain several seedlings, but each plant retains its own trunk.
sunlightInstructions: Medium indirect daylight works well; avoid strong direct sunlight.
wateringInstructions: Keep the mix from drying completely while allowing excess water to drain. Check conditions before adding more.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: A humus-rich potting mix with good drainage.
humidityInstructions: Normal comfortable room conditions suit it. Protect from extremes and inspect fronds for mites or scale.

description: A clustering palm with fan-shaped leaves and slender fibre-covered canes. The reference photo shows its mature form.
sunlightInstructions: Indirect light is suitable. It tolerates shade, but avoid a dark corner with no useful daylight.
wateringInstructions: Water regularly with good drainage, reducing frequency during winter.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: A well-drained indoor potting mix.
humidityInstructions: Ordinary room humidity is usually adequate. Leave space for the clump to spread and check for common houseplant pests.

description: A glossy-leaved tropical shrub grown indoors for foliage. Flowers and coffee cherries are not guaranteed indoors. Keep the plant and its caffeine-containing seeds away from pets.
sunlightInstructions: Give bright filtered light, with shelter from strong midday sun.
wateringInstructions: Keep the mix consistently moist but not soggy during growth. Reduce watering when growth slows.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: A rich, freely draining potting mix with organic matter.
humidityInstructions: Likes warm conditions and humid air. Protect from cold drafts and avoid drying out the roots.

description: A clumping plant with strap-like leaves and clusters of orange flowers. It often flowers best once established; a cool rest can help, but bloom timing varies.
sunlightInstructions: Filtered light or gentle morning sun suits indoor plants. Avoid harsh midday sun.
wateringInstructions: Let the surface start to dry between waterings. Reduce water during the cool resting period and keep water out of the crown.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: A well-drained potting mix; avoid unnecessary repotting of an established plant.
humidityInstructions: Give good air circulation. Keep the resting plant cool and sheltered from frost; do not force a fixed flowering timetable.

description: A trailing succulent with rounded bead-like leaves, formerly called Senecio rowleyanus. It suits a hanging pot with drainage.
sunlightInstructions: Bright indirect light indoors; protect from scorching direct sun.
wateringInstructions: Allow the upper mix to dry before watering carefully. Avoid both a permanently wet pot and prolonged complete dehydration.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: A freely draining cactus mix, with an open pot and drainage holes.
humidityInstructions: Ordinary indoor air is suitable. Give a brighter position rather than compensating for low light with extra water.

photo.title: Curio rowleyanus, string of pearls, houseplant view

description: A compact succulent forming pale blue-green rosettes and small offsets. Leaf colour and flowering vary with growing conditions.
sunlightInstructions: Choose a very bright window with some direct sun, acclimatizing gradually.
wateringInstructions: Let the mix dry between thorough waterings. Keep water out of the rosette and reduce watering in winter.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: A gritty, fast-draining succulent mix in a shallow pot with drainage.
humidityInstructions: Avoid humid, stagnant conditions and cold wet roots. Handle leaves gently to preserve their surface coating.

description: A small succulent with white raised bands on pointed leaves. It is often confused with Haworthiopsis fasciata; this species also has bumps on the inner leaf surface.
sunlightInstructions: Bright indirect daylight suits it; protect from scorching direct sun.
wateringInstructions: Allow the potting mix to dry between waterings, and drain thoroughly.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: A freely draining cactus or succulent mix.
humidityInstructions: Tolerates typical indoor humidity. Avoid cold drafts and water sitting between the leaves.

description: A compact plant with rounded, striped leaves and reddish stalks, formerly called Peperomia argyreia. It is a peperomia rather than a begonia.
sunlightInstructions: Provide bright indirect daylight without harsh direct sun.
wateringInstructions: Water when the top of the mix feels dry. Avoid both waterlogged roots and letting the whole pot remain very dry.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: A loose, well-drained houseplant mix in a pot with drainage.
humidityInstructions: Keep warm and away from cold drafts. It can remain in the same pot until roots genuinely need more space.

description: A slow-growing succulent with fuzzy pale leaves and brown markings along their edges. Different cultivars vary in colour and shape.
sunlightInstructions: Give strong indirect daylight, protecting it from very hot direct sun.
wateringInstructions: Allow the mix to dry between waterings. Water less during slow winter growth.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: A well-drained cactus or succulent mix.
humidityInstructions: Prefers drier air and a warm position. Avoid cold wet roots and keep water off the fuzzy leaves.

description: A compact foliage plant with pink, white or red speckles. Different cultivars have different patterns; pinching long stems can encourage a bushier shape.
sunlightInstructions: Bright filtered daylight supports the leaf colour. Protect from intense direct sun.
wateringInstructions: Keep the mix lightly moist with good drainage. Check the surface before watering and avoid waterlogged roots.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: A moist, freely draining houseplant mix.
humidityInstructions: A warm indoor position suits it. Watch for powdery mildew and give the foliage space for air circulation.

photo.title: Hypoestes phyllostachya, Polka Dot Plant, houseplant view

description: A sprawling plant whose leaves and stems are covered in purple hairs. Pinching stems can keep it bushier; its small orange flowers can have an unpleasant smell.
sunlightInstructions: Choose bright indirect daylight, sheltered from hot afternoon sun.
wateringInstructions: Keep the mix moist while growing, without leaving it soggy. Water less often in winter.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: A loose houseplant mix in a pot with drainage holes.
humidityInstructions: Keep in comfortable room conditions and inspect for mites or mealybugs. A hanging pot gives the weak stems room to spread.

photo.title: Gynura aurantiaca- Growing in a pot

description: A bromeliad with a leafy rosette and colourful bracts around small flowers. After flowering the main rosette declines, while offshoots can continue growing. Bract colour varies between cultivars.
sunlightInstructions: Use indirect daylight or suitable artificial lighting. Avoid harsh direct sun.
wateringInstructions: Water the roots sparingly and keep water in the central leaf cup during warm active growth. Refresh the cup water to avoid stagnation.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: An open bromeliad or orchid mix that allows air around the roots.
humidityInstructions: Prefers humid air with circulation. Do not keep the root zone waterlogged.

description: A broad-leaved shrub with deeply lobed leaves, grown indoors or in conservatories. The reference photograph shows a large outdoor specimen; indoor size depends on space and care.
sunlightInstructions: Choose indirect light or a shaded position with useful daylight. Strong direct sun can damage leaves.
wateringInstructions: Keep the mix moist with good drainage. Avoid a constantly saturated pot.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: A fertile, humus-rich, freely draining potting mix.
humidityInstructions: Allow room for spreading leaves. Check indoor plants for mites, scale and mealybugs; reduce feeding during winter.

description: An evergreen conifer with regularly tiered branches. It is grown as an indoor tree, but is not a true pine and can eventually outgrow a small room.
sunlightInstructions: Give a bright window position, with gentle sun where possible. Protect from intense afternoon sun and avoid a dark corner.
wateringInstructions: Water regularly during growth, letting excess drain. Reduce watering in winter and avoid persistently wet soil.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: A fertile, porous, slightly acidic mix with good drainage.
humidityInstructions: A bright, cooler room suits it. Allow height for the tree and avoid very dry conditions that can cause lower branches to drop.

photo.title: Araucaria heterophylla, Norfolk Island Pine, houseplant view

description: A woody foliage plant with leathery leaves in many shapes and colours. The photo is one cultivar. Keep away from pets, and avoid contact with the irritating sap.
sunlightInstructions: Needs strong daylight and some direct sun for good colour. Acclimatize to a brighter window gradually.
wateringInstructions: Water generously during growth with free drainage, allowing the mix to start drying. Water more sparingly in winter.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: A humus-rich, well-drained potting mix.
humidityInstructions: Keep warm and watch for spider mites. Handle damaged stems carefully and wash hands after contact with sap.

description: A trailing or climbing evergreen often grown in indoor pots. The photograph shows the variegated cultivar Gold Child. Leaves and berries are harmful if eaten and sap can irritate skin.
sunlightInstructions: Provide filtered daylight; variegated forms need enough light to retain their pattern.
wateringInstructions: Keep the mix moist with drainage, checking before watering rather than leaving the pot saturated.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: A fertile, well-drained houseplant mix.
humidityInstructions: Allow trailing stems space and inspect for mites or scale. Keep contained; it can spread aggressively if planted outdoors.

description: A grass-like sedge with umbrella-shaped whorls of bracts. Despite one common name it is not a palm. It needs wetter roots than most houseplants.
sunlightInstructions: Give bright light with protection from scorching sun.
wateringInstructions: Keep the roots wet at all times. The container can stand in a tray of water; do not use a dry-out routine.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: A fertile, moisture-retentive mix suited to a water-loving plant.
humidityInstructions: Protect the bracts from harsh drafts. Brown tips can result when roots dry; tall stems may need support.

description: A trailing tropical plant with glossy leaves and red tubular flowers. A hanging pot shows off its stems; flowering depends on growing conditions.
sunlightInstructions: Bright indirect light suits it. Avoid full, harsh sun.
wateringInstructions: Water regularly while growing and drain the pot. Keep a little drier in winter without leaving roots desiccated.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: An airy, well-drained mix for an epiphytic houseplant.
humidityInstructions: Likes warmth and humid air with good circulation. Avoid cold drafts, stagnant damp conditions and wet foliage.

description: A trailing tropical plant with small fleshy leaves and pouch-shaped orange flowers. It suits a hanging basket; it is distinct from other plants sold under the goldfish name.
sunlightInstructions: Choose bright filtered light, avoiding long exposure to full sun.
wateringInstructions: Keep the mix moist but freely draining, using soft water where available. Check moisture before watering.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: A peat-free, freely draining potting compost.
humidityInstructions: Keep warm and away from cold windows. Allow room for trailing stems and check for aphids.

description: A rhizomatous foliage begonia with dark cross-shaped markings on textured green leaves. It is grown mainly for foliage rather than its small flowers. Keep out of reach of pets.
sunlightInstructions: Bright filtered daylight, protected from strong direct sun.
wateringInstructions: Keep evenly moist during active growth, with good drainage. When growth slows, let the surface nearly dry before watering again.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: A moisture-retentive, freely draining houseplant mix.
humidityInstructions: Prefers warmth and humid air. Keep foliage dry and provide circulation; avoid overwatering the rhizome.

description: A clumping prayer-family plant with feather-like patterns on pale leaves and purple undersides. Leaves can fold in the evening; indoor flowers are uncommon.
sunlightInstructions: Bright indirect daylight or light shade, away from harsh direct sun.
wateringInstructions: Keep the mix moist without leaving it soggy. Use rainwater or distilled water where tap-water sensitivity is a problem.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: An organically rich mix with perlite or similar material for drainage.
humidityInstructions: Needs warm, humid conditions and protection from drafts. Gently wipe dusty leaves rather than keeping them wet.

description: A compact foliage plant with patterned leaves and reddish-purple undersides. Pink and cream markings vary between cultivars, so the reference photograph is one example.
sunlightInstructions: Choose bright indirect daylight; strong sun can scorch the leaves.
wateringInstructions: Keep the root zone moist but freely draining, avoiding both saturation and complete drying. Rainwater or distilled water can help with sensitive leaf tips.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: A slightly acidic, organically rich mix with reliable drainage.
humidityInstructions: Prefers warm, humid air. Avoid cold drafts and leave space for circulation; keep water off the foliage.

description: A clumping tropical foliage plant with burgundy leaf undersides. The photograph shows the variegated cultivar presented as Tricolor; other forms can be largely green.
sunlightInstructions: Indirect daylight or dappled shade suits it. Protect from direct sun.
wateringInstructions: Keep the mix moist with good drainage. Do not allow the roots to dry out or remain waterlogged.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: A moisture-retentive, well-drained houseplant mix.
humidityInstructions: Likes warm, humid conditions. Leaves may fold at night; inspect for mites and keep the pot away from drafts.

description: A clump-forming foliage plant with fine pale pink or white lines across dark leaves. Leaves can fold at night, and leaf colour changes as foliage matures.
sunlightInstructions: Bright indirect daylight or light shade, sheltered from strong sun.
wateringInstructions: Keep the mix moist with drainage, avoiding both complete drying and a permanently wet pot.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: A rich, airy mix suitable for moisture-loving houseplants.
humidityInstructions: Prefers warmth and humid air. Wipe dust gently and avoid wet leaves or cold drafts.

photo.title: Goeppertia ornata- Growing in a pot

description: A tropical climbing philodendron with glossy leaves and reddish colouring on stalks or leaf undersides. Appearance varies between forms and cultivars. Keep away from pets.
sunlightInstructions: Give indirect daylight and protect from direct sunlight.
wateringInstructions: Keep the mix moist with good drainage. Avoid waterlogging and water at the base rather than over the leaves.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: An organically rich, freely draining potting mix.
humidityInstructions: Warm, humid conditions suit it. Provide a pole or trellis for climbing and protect from cold drafts.

description: A rhizomatous plant with triangular leaflets that close at night. Purple and green forms exist. It can enter a dormant period; keep away from pets because of its oxalates.
sunlightInstructions: A bright window with some gentle sun or partial shade. Protect from excessive heat.
wateringInstructions: Allow the surface to dry between waterings. Reduce water during dormancy and wait for new growth before increasing it.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: A loamy potting mix with good drainage.
humidityInstructions: Keep in a comfortable room and check for a resting period when growth stops. Do not keep dormant rhizomes soaked.

description: A short-lived flowering plant with glossy leaves and purple-blue flowers with yellow centres. It is often kept as a seasonal potted plant and can be difficult to maintain after flowering.
sunlightInstructions: Choose filtered daylight or light shade. Avoid direct sun.
wateringInstructions: Keep the mix moist but well drained. Check regularly during flowering and avoid leaving water in the outer pot.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: An organically rich, well-drained potting mix.
humidityInstructions: Keep warm and sheltered from cold drafts. Flowering depends on conditions; do not expect the plant to remain in bloom indefinitely.

description: A vigorous vine with small leaves on juvenile climbing stems. It clings to supports and can mark porous surfaces. The photo shows an outdoor specimen; indoor fruiting is uncommon. Keep away from pets.
sunlightInstructions: Bright indirect daylight or partial shade, protected from afternoon sun.
wateringInstructions: Water regularly during growth with free drainage. Reduce watering from autumn into winter.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: A soil-based, organically rich potting mix with drainage.
humidityInstructions: Prefers humid air. Prune to contain growth and use a suitable support rather than letting roots attach to delicate surfaces.

description: An evergreen shrub also sold as a flowering potted plant. Creamy-white flowers can be single or double depending on the cultivar. Indoor care can be demanding; keep away from pets.
sunlightInstructions: Bright indirect daylight or partial shade, sheltered from harsh sun.
wateringInstructions: Keep the mix moist with good drainage, checking before adding water. Avoid a saturated pot.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause feeding when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: A rich, acidic, freely draining mix; avoid disturbing the shallow roots unnecessarily.
humidityInstructions: Protect from cold drafts and abrupt changes. Watch for whiteflies and remove spent flowers; flowering is not guaranteed indoors.

description: A small air plant that attaches to a support instead of rooting in soil. The photo shows a mounted clump; leaf colour varies by cultivar and may redden around flowering.
sunlightInstructions: Give bright indirect daylight with protection from harsh sun.
wateringInstructions: Wet the leaves thoroughly, then gently shake off trapped water and allow the plant to dry with good air movement. Check regularly; humid air alone does not replace watering.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth, using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: Do not plant in ordinary potting soil. Use an open mount or holder that lets water drain and air reach the plant.
humidityInstructions: Prefers humid air with ventilation. Keep water from remaining trapped in the leaf bases. Offshoots can form clumps over time.

description: An epiphytic fern with forked, antler-like fronds and shield fronds covering its roots. The reference shows a tree-mounted specimen; it can also grow indoors on a mount.
sunlightInstructions: Provide filtered daylight or partial shade, avoiding scorching direct sun.
wateringInstructions: Water the root area regularly. Let it dry slightly between waterings, without letting it become completely dry. Drain thoroughly after watering.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth, using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: Use an airy epiphytic orchid or sphagnum moss mixture, or a suitable wood or bark mount; keep drainage open.
humidityInstructions: Prefers humid conditions with air movement. Mature shield fronds naturally turn brown; leave them in place rather than treating this as a diagnosis of damage.

description: A rainforest cactus with slender trailing stems, suited to a hanging pot. The reference shows stems and pale berries; indoor flowering and fruiting are not guaranteed.
sunlightInstructions: Bright indirect daylight, sheltered from harsh direct sun.
wateringInstructions: Water when the mix feels dry, then drain well. This rainforest cactus needs more consistent moisture than desert cacti; reduce watering in winter and avoid waterlogging.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth, using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: Use a slightly acidic, gritty, freely draining cactus mix in a pot with drainage holes.
humidityInstructions: Prefers humid air and good circulation. Avoid hot, arid conditions and prolonged drought.

description: A compact foliage plant with raised silver patches on green leaves. It is distinct from watermelon peperomia, despite their similar common names.
sunlightInstructions: Bright indirect daylight, protected from full sun.
wateringInstructions: Water moderately while growing, allowing good drainage. Reduce watering from autumn through late winter and avoid leaving the roots saturated.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth, using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: Use a moisture-retentive but freely draining indoor potting mix in a pot with drainage holes.
humidityInstructions: Prefers a warm, humid room with air circulation. Pinch stem tips for a bushier shape; overwatering and poor drainage can cause root rot.

description: A trailing houseplant grown for purple stems and narrow purple leaves. The reference shows Purple Heart foliage. Its sap can irritate skin and mouths; keep away from pets.
sunlightInstructions: Give a bright position with some direct sun, introducing stronger light gradually. Shadier conditions can produce greener foliage.
wateringInstructions: Water the mix and let excess drain. Check moisture before watering again; avoid a continually wet pot. Water less when growth slows.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth, using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: Use a well-drained potting mix with organic matter and a pot with drainage holes.
humidityInstructions: Protect from cold; bring container plants indoors before temperatures fall below 10 C. Pinching encourages branching; handle fragile stems carefully and avoid contact with sap.

description: A compact foliage plant with deeply ridged, heart-shaped leaves and slender cream flower spikes. Leaf colours vary between cultivars.
sunlightInstructions: Medium filtered daylight suits this plant. Protect from harsh direct sun and cold drafts.
wateringInstructions: Let the mix dry between waterings without leaving it severely dry. Water and drain thoroughly; avoid a constantly wet pot.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: Use a porous, freely draining indoor potting mix and a pot with drainage holes.
humidityInstructions: Ordinary indoor humidity is tolerated. Avoid drafty positions and watch for root rot if the mix stays wet.

description: A compact, trailing pilea with crinkled leaves and bronze-green colouring. The reference photo shows foliage and tiny flowers; indoor flowering is uncommon.
sunlightInstructions: Provide bright indirect daylight, sheltered from harsh sun.
wateringInstructions: Water moderately during growth and drain well. Reduce watering from autumn through late winter; avoid a saturated pot.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: Use an organically rich indoor potting mix with good drainage.
humidityInstructions: Prefers a warm, humid room. Pinch stem tips to keep a compact form; stem cuttings can produce new plants.

description: A creeping plant with tiny rounded leaves that form a soft-looking mat. It is a flowering plant rather than a moss and can crowd other plants in a terrarium.
sunlightInstructions: Bright indirect daylight. Direct sunlight can scorch its delicate leaves.
wateringInstructions: Keep the mix moist with free drainage. Check often in a warm room instead of waiting for the pot to become dry.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: Use fertile, moisture-retentive, well-drained mix. A wide, shallow pot suits its spreading habit.
humidityInstructions: Prefers high humidity and moderate temperatures. Trim spreading stems to keep it within its container.

description: A delicate fern with small fan-shaped leaflets on dark, wiry stems. The reference shows an outdoor specimen; it can be grown indoors in humid conditions.
sunlightInstructions: Provide filtered light or partial shade. Avoid full sun and very deep shade.
wateringInstructions: Keep the root area consistently moist. Do not allow the roots to dry out; check conditions frequently while retaining drainage.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: Use a moisture-retentive indoor potting mix in a pot with drainage.
humidityInstructions: Needs humid air; a bright bathroom or suitable terrarium may help. Protect from drying air and hot radiators.

description: An upright, branching succulent with three-sided stems and sharp spines. It resembles a cactus but is a euphorbia. Its milky sap is toxic and irritating; keep away from pets and children.
sunlightInstructions: Bright indirect daylight indoors, avoiding an abrupt move into harsh sun.
wateringInstructions: Water sparingly after the upper 2 to 5 cm of mix feels dry, then drain completely. Avoid overwatering.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: Use a freely draining cactus or succulent mix in a pot with drainage holes.
humidityInstructions: Keep warm with air circulation. Wear gloves when handling and avoid sap contact, particularly with eyes; handle the spines carefully.

photo.title: Euphorbia trigona or African milk tree, houseplant view

description: A saxifrage with white-veined leaves and thin runners that carry plantlets. It is neither a true begonia nor a strawberry. The reference shows an outdoor flowering specimen.
sunlightInstructions: Bright indirect daylight indoors, protected from intense direct sun.
wateringInstructions: Keep the mix moist while letting excess water drain. Check before adding more water and avoid leaving the pot saturated.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: Use an organically rich, well-drained potting mix.
humidityInstructions: Give spreading runners space in a hanging pot. Plantlets can root in soil; indoor flowering is not guaranteed.

description: A dracaena commonly sold as shaped green canes. It is not true bamboo. The photo shows canes growing in water; this plant can also grow in potting mix. Keep away from pets.
sunlightInstructions: Bright indirect daylight indoors, sheltered from scorching sun.
wateringInstructions: In potting mix, keep roots moist while avoiding waterlogging. For water-grown plants, use chlorine-free water and replace it weekly rather than only topping it up.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: Use a moist indoor potting mix, or grow in chlorine-free water with suitable support. The two growing methods need different care.
humidityInstructions: Keep warm and watch for stem rot. Dry air can brown leaf tips; shaped stems are trained forms, not a natural growth stage.

description: A slow-growing dracaena with cream or yellow spots on dark green leaves. Spotting varies by cultivar and light. Keep away from pets.
sunlightInstructions: Bright indirect daylight. Excessive sun can damage leaves; very low light can reduce the colouring.
wateringInstructions: Keep the mix moist during active growth, with good drainage. Avoid standing water and a continually saturated pot.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: Use a well-drained indoor potting mix and avoid an oversized container.
humidityInstructions: Prefers humid air and protection from drafts. Bring container plants indoors before nights fall below 10 C.

description: A prickly succulent shrub with small flowers surrounded by colourful bracts. Its sap is irritating and its spines are sharp; keep away from pets and children.
sunlightInstructions: A sunny indoor position suits this plant. Introduce stronger light gradually.
wateringInstructions: Let the mix dry between waterings and drain thoroughly. Avoid cold, wet soil, especially when growth slows.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: Use a freely draining soil-based mix in a pot with drainage holes.
humidityInstructions: Keep warm and handle carefully with gloves to avoid the spines and sap. Protect eyes and skin from sap contact.

description: A succulent shrub with a swollen stem base and showy flowers. The reference shows a large potted specimen; indoor size and flowering vary. Its milky sap is poisonous; keep away from pets.
sunlightInstructions: Give a sunny position, introducing strong light gradually.
wateringInstructions: Let the mix dry between waterings. Water during active growth and reduce watering during dormancy; never leave the pot saturated.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: Use a cactus or succulent mix in a pot with several drainage holes.
humidityInstructions: Keep warm and protect from cold. Handle the plant carefully and avoid contact with its milky sap.

description: A shrubby succulent with rounded blue-grey leaves and reddish edges. It is distinct from the green-leaved jade plant, Crassula ovata. The reference is a leaf detail. Keep away from pets.
sunlightInstructions: Full sun to light shade; introduce stronger indoor sun gradually.
wateringInstructions: Allow the mix to dry between waterings and drain well. Avoid overwatering and reduce watering when growth slows.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: Use a freely draining cactus or succulent mix and a pot with drainage holes.
humidityInstructions: Avoid a constantly damp pot. Watch for mealybugs; flowering is uncommon indoors.

description: A climbing hoya with thick heart-shaped leaves. A single rooted leaf may not develop into a vine unless the cutting includes suitable stem tissue. The photo shows a vining specimen.
sunlightInstructions: Give filtered daylight, sheltered from harsh direct sun.
wateringInstructions: Use room-temperature water, allowing the mix to dry somewhat between thorough waterings. Drain well and avoid a persistently wet pot.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: Use an airy, freely draining mix in a container with drainage holes.
humidityInstructions: Prefers warm, humid conditions. Provide a support or hanging pot; bare twining stems can later carry leaves and flowers.

description: A terrestrial orchid grown for its patterned leaves as well as small white flowers. It grows along creeping stems rather than attaching itself to a tree like many other orchids.
sunlightInstructions: Moderate filtered daylight or shade, avoiding harsh sun.
wateringInstructions: Keep the mix moist with good drainage. Water consistently with tepid water, without leaving roots or stems in wet soil.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: Use a moisture-retentive, well-drained mix suitable for terrestrial orchids in a wide, shallow pot.
humidityInstructions: Prefers warm, humid air with good circulation. Avoid waterlogged mix, which can rot roots and stems.

description: A climbing aroid whose leaves can become deeply divided as it develops. The photo shows the Albo form; Cebu Blue is another cultivar. Leaf colour and splitting vary. Keep away from pets.
sunlightInstructions: Bright indirect daylight in a warm position, protected from cold drafts.
wateringInstructions: Keep the mix moist while allowing excess water to drain. Check before watering again and avoid a saturated pot.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: Use an organically rich, well-drained indoor mix with drainage holes.
humidityInstructions: Prefers moderate humidity. Give climbing stems a suitable support and prune to keep the plant within its space.

photo.title: Epipremnum pinnatum 'Albo' houseplant view with young leaves

description: A large foliage plant with deeply lobed leaves, also known as Thaumatophyllum bipinnatifidum. The reference shows Selloum. Allow room for spreading leaves; keep away from pets.
sunlightInstructions: Bright filtered daylight; protect from scorching full sun.
wateringInstructions: Keep the mix moist with good drainage. Avoid both prolonged drought and a constantly saturated pot.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: Use an organically rich, well-drained indoor mix and a stable pot with drainage.
humidityInstructions: Prefers moderate humidity and warmth. It can outgrow small rooms; foliage shape varies with growing conditions.

description: A tropical foliage shrub with leaves that may be green, pink, purple or red depending on the cultivar. The reference shows patterned foliage. Keep away from pets.
sunlightInstructions: Bright indirect daylight helps maintain the leaf colours.
wateringInstructions: Water regularly, allowing the mix to dry slightly between waterings. Reduce watering from late autumn through winter and avoid a soggy pot.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: Use fertile, moisture-retentive but well-drained indoor potting mix.
humidityInstructions: Prefers warm, humid air and protection from drafts. Avoid cold conditions and wear gloves if handling sap.

description: A slow-growing cycad with stiff, palm-like fronds, rather than a true palm. The reference shows spiny lower leaflets. All parts are highly poisonous, especially seeds; keep away from pets and children.
sunlightInstructions: Bright filtered daylight indoors, protected from harsh direct sun.
wateringInstructions: Maintain moisture with excellent drainage, checking before watering. Avoid overwatering and do not leave the roots in a saturated pot.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: Use a well-drained, sandy or loamy mix in a pot with drainage holes.
humidityInstructions: Protect from frost and handle the spiny foliage carefully. Indoor plants rarely produce cones, and the photo is not a mature-size or growth-timeline target.

photo.title: Lower leaflets are often spine like in the Cycadaceae family.

description: A climbing vine with glossy, three-part leaves and grasping tendrils. Grow it on a support or let stems trail from a hanging pot.
sunlightInstructions: Provide bright, indirect daylight. Keep it out of harsh direct sun.
wateringInstructions: Allow the surface mix to dry between waterings, then drain thoroughly. Reduce watering in winter; avoid both prolonged dryness and a saturated pot.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: Use a well-drained indoor potting mix in a container with drainage holes.
humidityInstructions: Ordinary indoor humidity is tolerated. Keep away from heating vents and cold drafts; prune trailing growth to suit the space.

description: A fern with finely divided fronds and fuzzy rhizomes that creep over the pot edge. These exposed rhizomes are a normal growth feature.
sunlightInstructions: Give indirect daylight, protected from scorching sun.
wateringInstructions: Keep the mix lightly moist, allowing the top centimetre to dry before watering again. Drain well rather than leaving the pot in water.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: Use a moisture-retentive, well-drained fern mix. Let the creeping rhizomes rest on the surface rather than burying them.
humidityInstructions: Prefers humid air, although it tolerates drier rooms better than some ferns. Keep warm and protect from cold drafts.

description: A creeping houseplant with patterned leaves and small tubular flowers. Leaf colours vary by cultivar; the reference photo shows Silver Sheen.
sunlightInstructions: Provide plentiful bright, indirect daylight. Direct sun can scorch the leaves.
wateringInstructions: Water the mix moderately to keep it lightly moist during active growth. Reduce watering in winter and avoid wetting the leaves or leaving roots waterlogged.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: Use a freely draining houseplant mix and a pot with drainage holes.
humidityInstructions: Needs humid air with good circulation. A suitable terrarium can help maintain humidity; do not rely on spraying the leaves.

description: A small trailing plant with soft leaves and violet trumpet-shaped flowers. It is a different species from the familiar rosette-forming African violet.
sunlightInstructions: Choose a bright, sheltered position with filtered light. Avoid harsh midday sun.
wateringInstructions: Let the potting mix dry somewhat between waterings, then drain well. Its shallow roots are vulnerable to excessive watering.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: Use a well-drained, organically rich mix in a pot with drainage holes.
humidityInstructions: Keep warm with good air circulation and protection from drying drafts. Remove spent flowers and unhealthy foliage.

description: A vigorous climbing vine with toothed green leaves. It can trail from a basket or climb a support; pruning helps keep it within an indoor space.
sunlightInstructions: Filtered daylight or partial shade is suitable. Protect it from harsh sun.
wateringInstructions: Allow the mix to dry between waterings, then drain thoroughly. Adjust checks to room conditions; both excess water and prolonged dryness can cause leaf loss.
fertilizingInstructions: Feed only during active growth using a suitable product label. Reduce or pause when growth slows; add a reminder only if needed.
soilInstructions: Use a freely draining indoor potting mix and a pot with drainage holes.
humidityInstructions: Keep away from heating vents and drafts. Avoid repeatedly moving an established plant; a cooler room can suit its winter rest.

description: A warm-season crop with many bush and climbing forms. Choose a variety suited to your space and local growing season. Leaves and stems are not food.
sunlightInstructions: Choose a sunny growing site; shelter and seasonal conditions matter. Follow the growing notes for this crop.
wateringInstructions: Check soil moisture regularly and keep it even, watering the soil rather than the foliage. Containers can dry quickly in warm weather.
fertilizingInstructions: Base feeding on soil or container needs and a suitable product label. Do not feed automatically during dormancy.
soilInstructions: Use fertile, well-drained soil or a large pot with drainage.
humidityInstructions: Provide air circulation and check outdoor weather or greenhouse conditions. Avoid leaving roots waterlogged.

catalogProfile.growingNotes: Start seedlings under cover and move outside only after frost risk has passed. Follow the variety label for support and side-shoot pruning.
catalogProfile.harvestInstructions: Pick sound fruit when it reaches its variety's ripe colour. Keep foliage away from pets.

photo.title: Solanum lycopersicum grown in porous terracotta pots on a porch.

description: A dwarf bush tomato producing small red cherry tomatoes. This is a cultivar of tomato, suitable for sunny containers.
sunlightInstructions: Choose a sunny growing site; shelter and seasonal conditions matter. Follow the growing notes for this crop.
wateringInstructions: Keep the root zone evenly moist with free drainage; check containers often in warm weather.
fertilizingInstructions: Base feeding on soil or container needs and a suitable product label. Do not feed automatically during dormancy.
soilInstructions: Use a drained container filled with fertile growing mix.
humidityInstructions: Provide air circulation and check outdoor weather or greenhouse conditions. Avoid leaving roots waterlogged.

catalogProfile.growingNotes: Protect from frost. This bush cultivar does not require routine side-shoot removal.
catalogProfile.harvestInstructions: Pick ripe red fruit regularly. Leaves and stems are not edible.

description: A plum tomato cultivar grown for red fruits often used in sauces. Check the supplier's label for its growth habit and training needs.
sunlightInstructions: Choose a sunny growing site; shelter and seasonal conditions matter. Follow the growing notes for this crop.
wateringInstructions: Keep the growing mix consistently moist while allowing excess water to drain.
fertilizingInstructions: Base feeding on soil or container needs and a suitable product label. Do not feed automatically during dormancy.
soilInstructions: Use fertile, freely draining soil or a generous drained container.
humidityInstructions: Provide air circulation and check outdoor weather or greenhouse conditions. Avoid leaving roots waterlogged.

catalogProfile.growingNotes: Choose a sunny, sheltered place after frost risk has passed. Support fruit-bearing stems as needed.
catalogProfile.harvestInstructions: Pick fully coloured, sound fruits for fresh use or cooking. Do not eat leaves or stems.
